meta.title: Thai B1 Intermediate
meta.subtitle: 1000 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Thai → English (see the Thai, recall the meaning) and English → Thai (see an English meaning, recall the Thai). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 1000 words for an intermediate learner, aligned to B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand the main points of clear standard input on familiar matters regularly encountered in work, school, leisure, etc.' — a learner here is able to deal with most situations likely to arise while travelling, to produce simple connected text on familiar topics, and to describe experiences and events, dreams, hopes and ambitions, and briefly give reasons and explanations for opinions and plans. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Thai, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 436 of the 1000 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — work and careers, money, banking and the economy, education, the news, media and technology, government, law and society, the environment, health and medicine, travel, transport and accommodation, the household and its chores, relationships and the stages of life, feelings and character, religion, Buddhism and Thai customs, the royal and polite registers a learner meets, abstract nouns for ideas, reasons and plans, the connectors that join sentences, and the verbs of thinking, deciding, arguing and changing — and the other 564 are the commonest remaining words of Thai, taken from the word counts of the Thai National Corpus, a large collection of written Thai. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in Thai script with a romanisation beneath it in the Paiboon system, which marks the TONE on every syllable — no mark for mid, à low, â falling, á high, ǎ rising — because a Thai word said on the wrong tone is a different word; the Thai Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script and the rules that decide a tone. 103 nouns show the classifier they are counted with (a house is counted in หลัง, an animal in ตัว), and there are no forms to learn: Thai words never change shape. Example sentences come with 548 of the 1000 words, three apiece for 228 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, romanisation, classifiers and some example sentences: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: the Thai National Corpus word list as distributed by PyThaiNLP (CC0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
